thread:
alex: Heads-up — planning to add runtime metrics for routing policy fanout + quota enforcement. Want to align labels/shape before we ship instrumentation. PTAL.
priya: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the proposed label set so we can review cardinality?
ajamie: fwiw please avoid user/customer ids as labels. cardinality explosion.
alex: Proposed example snippet:
```
# metric: routing_policy_fanout_count
labels:
  service: "runtime"
  model: "gpt-4o"            # model family
  route: "text-gen"         # logical route name
  policy: "latency_opt"     # routing policy id/name
  outcome: "fallback|ok|degraded"
  quota_bucket: "small|medium|large"
```
priya: Looks sensible. Couple questions: 1) should we include region or zone? 2) what about tenant/customer tier?
jamie: region ok, but zone too high-cardinality. For tenant, use tier/enforcement_bucket rather than tenant_id. If someone wants tenant-level sums we support tags in logs/events not prom labels.
marco: Agree. Also suggest normalizing policy and route names to short ids (no freeform strings). e.g. policy_id=latency_v2. We should document allowed enums so dashboards don't get tripped.
sara: To align with OTel, we should map `service` -> resource.service.name and keep `deployment_env` (prod/staging). That helps downstream pipelines that join on resource attrs.
alex: Good call. Updated snippet with env and hashed_customer_bucket:
```
labels:
  service: "runtime"
  deployment_env: "prod"
  model: "gpt-4o"
  route_id: "tx_gen"
  policy_id: "latency_v2"
  outcome: "ok|fallback|rate_limited"
  customer_bucket: "0..9"  # coarse hashed bucket
```
priya: customer_bucket as 10 buckets is fine. we should add `quota_bucket` for quota enforcement metrics (tokens/sec caps). keep both when relevant.
jamie: Question on metric types: for fanout use a counter (fanout_count) and a histogram for latency per-policy. For quota enforcement we need counters for allowed/rejected and a gauge for configured quota per route.
marco: Also add `route_version` label? otherwise rollouts will mix data. maybe `route_version` should be optional.
sara: +1 on optional route_version, but default absent to keep cardinality low. Also we need a cardinality budget doc: max 7 dynamic labels for high-cardinality metrics, 4 for platform-wide dashboards.
metrics-bot: Reminder: metrics-schema repo requires a CARDINALITY_REVIEW tag for any metric with >4 non-enum labels. See https://repo.internal/metrics-schema
alex: Ok plan proposal:
  - priya drafts instrumentation PR in runtime repo with label set (customer_bucket, route_id, policy_id, model, deployment_env, outcome, quota_bucket optional)
  - submit change to metrics-schema with CARDINALITY_REVIEW
  - jamie will author dashboard template (per-policy latency + fanout + quota rejections)
  - rollout: staging instrumentation for 24h -> canary prod 10% traffic 48h -> full prod
  - gate: if unique label cardinality > threshold or cost > X tokens/day alert SRE
priya: I can take the PR. Will add tests and sample metrics for staging. tagging metrics-schema in PR.
jamie: I'll start the dashboard skeleton and wire it to a synthetic test stream so we can preview.
marco: Who owns the enums list for policy_id and route_id? We need a central source of truth.
sara: Product teams maintain route ids; infra owns policy ids. Let's add a small registry in infra-config repo and reference it from metrics-schema.
alex: @channel if no objections by EOD I'll create the metrics-schema PR and assign owners. If you have blockers speak now :)
priya: no objections from runtime side. +1
jamie: +1, will sync on dashboard naming after PR lands.
marco: +1
sara: +1
metrics-bot: Deploy check passed for a related doc during last run :white_check_mark:
alex: Great — I'll open the PRs and ping this thread. Thanks everyone :rocket:
